summary:
Team EQUINOX built Earth System Trend Detective, a bilingual (Arabic/English) 3D web platform powered by FastAPI, SciPy/Statsmodels, and React 18 + Three.js (react-globe.gl).

What We Developed: Using 26+ years of NASA Earth observations (2000–2026) across 16+ variables (GLDAS, GPM IMERG, MODIS, MERRA-2, AIRS, OMI, and live NASA POWER API), our hybrid engine delivers < 19.6ms telemetry, spherical w = cos(lat) area weighting, a dual time-series lab with a 5y–26y sensitivity slider, and 4 zero-hallucination AI agents (biome recommender, bilingual narrator, NL 3D-camera orchestrator, and STL anomaly detector).

How It Addresses the Challenge: It directly answers NASA's four questions (What, Where, How Much, Is It Significant?) by running deseasonalized Hamed-Rao Mann-Kendall (p < 0.0001), Theil-Sen slopes, and STL decomposition (|Z| >= 1.8σ/2σ) across 8 coupled teleconnections—like +NAO drying Jordan (-3.42 kg/m²/dec) while wetting Northern Europe (+4.1 kg/m²/dec, r = -0.944).

Why It's Important: With NASA EOSDIS exceeding 170+ PB (500–600 PB by 2030) in complex NetCDF/HDF5 formats, our zero-code tool lets policymakers, educators, farmers, researchers, and journalists separate weather noise from real climate shifts in seconds.
details:
Here is a copy-paste-ready response covering all six NASA Space Apps submission questions in plain text (without bold formatting):

1. What does it do and how does it work?

Earth System Trend Detective (developed by Team EQUINOX) is an interactive, bilingual (English and Arabic) 3D web platform that turns over 26 years of NASA Earth observation archives (2000–2026) into instant, statistically verified climate trend analysis without requiring any programming.

It works through a 3-stage pipeline:

- Stage 1 (Hybrid Data Ingestion): Pre-verified multi-decadal NASA Data Rods (demo_timeseries_cache.json) load in under 19.6 milliseconds across 16+ variables and 4 Earth spheres (GLDAS Noah025 v2.1, GPM IMERG v07, MODIS MOD11C3/MOD13C2/MYD28M/AOD/Sea Ice, MERRA-2, Aqua AIRS, and Aura OMI). For any custom latitude/longitude outside the cache, FastAPI asynchronously queries the live NASA POWER API via parallel asyncio.gather requests. Regional aggregations in Hotspot, Buffer, and Bounding-Box modes apply spherical latitude area-weighting w = cos(lat) so high-latitude grid cells do not distort regional averages.

- Stage 2 (Deterministic Statistical Engine + 4 Zero-Hallucination AI Agents): Python (SciPy and Statsmodels) runs deseasonalized Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall trend tests (correcting serial autocorrelation), outlier-resistant Theil-Sen median slopes, t-tests, 95% confidence bands, and STL Loess decomposition (AI #4) to isolate seasonal noise and flag extreme anomaly years (|Z| >= 1.8 sigma / +-2 sigma). Three additional AI modules operate strictly on those computed metrics: AI #1 recommends the Top 3 NASA variables for any clicked biome (98% match), AI #2 writes bilingual Arabic/English reports locked to computed p, r, and slope values, and AI #3 converts natural Arabic or English queries into dual-region locks and 3D globe camera flights.

- Stage 3 (Interactive 3D Liquid Glass Client): Built in React 18 and Three.js (react-globe.gl), users explore a 60fps 3D globe showing 8 coupled teleconnection pairs (such as +NAO, ENSO, +IOD, and Sahara-Amazon), compare two regions side by side in the Dual Time-Series Lab with an animated Teleconnection Seesaw, test short-window bias using a 5-to-26-year Sensitivity Slider, and export 1-click 3x PNG Bento Case Cards, PDF reports, and Miro Workflow Boards.

2. What benefits does it have?

- Eliminates format lock-in: Bridges NASA's 170+ PB EOSDIS archive (projected to reach 500–600 PB by 2030) out of NetCDF/HDF5/GRIB files into an accessible, zero-code browser experience.

- Separates weather noise from climate signals: Prevents false positives caused by 3-to-7-year natural cycles (ENSO, +NAO) and extreme single-year spikes.

- Reveals opposite regional dipoles: Shows how a single planetary mode (+NAO) drives simultaneous opposite effects—for example, drying root-zone soil moisture in Jordan and the Levant (-3.42 kg/m2/decade) while wetting Northern Europe (+4.1 kg/m2/decade) with an inverse correlation of r = -0.944 and p < 0.0001.

- Dual-audience accessibility: Serves students with a Guided Variable Funnel and +XP learning rewards, while giving researchers a full NASA Tech Drawer, Sensitivity Matrix, and instant export tools.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to democratize NASA Earth science for the 99% of decision-makers who do not write Python or JavaScript—empowering policymakers and water authorities to verify watershed trends before allocating budgets, educators and students to visualize global teleconnections in 3D, agricultural planners and NGOs to monitor 26-year soil moisture and NDVI trajectories, data journalists to fact-check climate claims with 1-click verified case cards, and researchers to perform sub-20ms exploratory screening before downloading gigabytes of raw granules. Built in full compliance with NASA Policy Directive SPD-41a, the platform also supports a sustainable Freemium SaaS model ($0 Community Tier alongside B2B/B2G Pro SaaS, Risk APIs, and EdTech institutional licenses).

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

- Backend & Statistical Engine: Python, FastAPI, SciPy, Statsmodels, NumPy, asyncio, NASA POWER API, and pre-indexed NASA Data Rods (demo_timeseries_cache.json).

- Frontend & 3D Visualization: JavaScript/TypeScript, React 18, Three.js, react-globe.gl, Recharts, Framer Motion, HTML5, and CSS3 (Apple iOS 18 / visionOS Liquid Glass design system with bilingual English and Arabic RTL support).

- AI & Export Workflow: 4 specialized AI detective modules (Biome Recommender, Statistical Narrator, Bilingual Spotlight NL Orchestrator, and STL Anomaly ML), Miro Workflow Board integration, and 3x PNG / PDF export pipelines.

- Hardware & Environment: Standard team laptops/workstations and modern WebGL-enabled browsers running local FastAPI (:8000) and React (:5173) development servers.

5. How is your project creative?

- Unifying 3D intuition with rigorous non-parametric math: Existing tools split the workflow—NASA Eyes/Worldview offer 3D visuals without trend math, while NASA Giovanni and Google Earth Engine offer math in 2D or require code. We fused a 60fps 3D teleconnection globe with Hamed-Rao Mann-Kendall, Theil-Sen, and STL math in a single zero-code interface.

- Interactive Teleconnection Seesaw & 5y–26y Sensitivity Slider: Instead of static charts, users physically see two distant basins tilt in opposite directions and can drag a time-window slider to watch how short 5-year windows create misleading trends compared to 26-year evidence.

- Zero-hallucination AI architecture: Rather than letting LLMs invent numbers, Python deterministically computes every statistic first and constrains the AI agents to explain, route, and visualize verified results in both Arabic and English.

6. What factors did your team consider?

- Statistical validity: Correcting monthly hydrological autocorrelation via Hamed & Rao (1998) to avoid 30–40% false-positive inflation, and using Sen (1968) median slopes for outlier immunity.

- Geospatial accuracy: Applying w = cos(lat) spherical area weighting across Buffer and Bounding-Box modes so high-latitude regions (such as 50N–70N) are not distorted.

- Performance & reliability: Pairing a < 19.6ms cached Data Rod layer with live asynchronous NASA POWER API fallback so demos and custom global queries stay fast and resilient.

- Inclusivity & bilingual UX: Full Arabic RTL and English support alongside plain-language student funnels and gamified +XP loops.

- Legal & scientific transparency: Following NASA SPD-41a open-data attribution rules and clearly recognizing current 0.25–0.5 degree monthly resolution bounds (with a post-hackathon roadmap for 10m–30m HLS/ECOSTRESS downscaling and Earthdata Cloud Zarr streaming).
